range_convention: One-based inclusive lines, original line endings, SHA-256 of excerpt bytes. Dependencies refer to the manuscript claims in this module.

claims.title: The first torsion layer of the level-two even-twist Selmer group is the dual of a cyclotomic class-group eigenspace
The fixed-field CorGK estimate at the principal target bounds the primes carrying each indicated even eigenspace
The marked element of an integral lift splits into three labelled lines functorially over the complete local coefficient ring
At the admitted characteristic-eleven datum the exterior constituents violate the published individual-polarization hypothesis
No CM restriction and common twist of the split residual triple satisfies both individual polarization and multiplicity one
Generic support suffices on each relevant component and a finite free two-branch family shows why crossing needs an arithmetic input
At every auxiliary prime the strict level condition follows from unramifiedness for a character of order prime to the coefficient prime
All characters in a prime-to-order orbit are distinct integral summands of the same twisted Selmer group
One finite even K-group of the character field bounds all eligible orbit lengths and their prime-weighted sum
Strict character lengths are finite even at a prime dividing the character order and in residue characteristic two
The entire generic orbit has length equal to the primitive K-group length, giving the least integer allowed by the valuation tests
The first layer on the character field with roots of unity is class-group duality, and the reflected odd unit space gives a vanishing test
Four arithmetic tests give zero strict length for entire families of trivial-character twists
The existing large-prime torsion estimate supplies a polynomial level bound at bounded twist and degree and leaves an explicit rate requirement
The total local correction between the strict groups and the even K-group of a CM host is at most polynomial in its degree and twist
Descent through ramified CM primes and the higher class number formulas identify the critical sign at every odd prime
Integral Bernoulli values and higher roots of unity give a single small integer for all the odd valuations of the critical sign
Every cyclotomic CM host satisfies the full odd-minus estimate with zero exceptional-prime term
The original window sum differs from the logarithm of the dyadic and complementary odd K-group orders by explicit small errors
Over the ninth cyclotomic field the odd-minus strict group at twist two has order thirteen and contributes at that prime alone
The simultaneous interval bounds the complete dyadic K-group order on the actual CM host
Odd-primary descent on every subfield of the host and restriction to the fixed reference layer control the invariant strict summand
Integral projectors decompose each odd same-sign K-group into the base and primitive ratios for at most four cyclic fields at each higher level
The full height sum on the simultaneous window is bounded on both sides by the odd cyclic-field product with explicit errors
The degree-sixteen host with quadratic conductors three and seven exhibits every kernel, predecessor and conjugation sign in the factorization
The strict polarized lower triangular tangent space has an unrestricted adjacent entry and a negative central entry
The central strict tangent lengths at every odd finite coefficient level satisfy the uniform odd-minus bound on the host
Each pure adjacent sign integrates in a triangular polynomial family, and the positive sign also satisfies the original mark normalization
At level two a quotient of the even cyclotomic class group gives distinct strict marked classes, with at most one dimension lost at two
The obstruction to integrating mixed adjacent signs is an explicit negative cup class locally zero at the prescribed places
Finite global duality and the rank of odd K-groups bound the entire negative mixed obstruction group independently of the auxiliary places
